regimen_profiles.context_label: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Carboplatin every 3 weeks with head and neck radiotherapy
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Carboplatin is given with radiotherapy to treat locally advanced head and neck cancer when cisplatin is unsuitable. Your team explains the intended chance of cure or long-term control for your diagnosis.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Locally advanced stage III–IV head and neck squamous cell carcinoma when cisplatin is not appropriate.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Carboplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with DNA copying and repair. This can stop cancer cells dividing. Normal blood-forming cells can also be affected, and kidney function determines how the medicine is cleared. Radiotherapy directs radiation at a carefully planned area. It is delivered on its own appointment calendar. Effects depend on which tissues receive radiation and can build up during the course or continue after it finishes.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Carboplatin is given through a vein over about 30 minutes on Day 1 every 21 days. The head and neck prescription uses AUC 5, a target used with your checked kidney function to calculate the dose. The whole visit includes safety checks, anti-sickness medicines, preparation and observation. Three carboplatin cycles are planned with concurrent radiotherapy. Radiation has a separate appointment calendar; the team coordinates any interruptions or changes.
key_points: Locally advanced stage III–IV head and neck squamous cell carcinoma when cisplatin is not appropriate.

Discuss your diagnosis, intent, alternatives, expected benefit and uncertainty, treatment burden, serious or lasting harms, fertility and pregnancy precautions and your priorities. Include blood-count suppression, serious infection and bleeding, nausea/vomiting, allergy, renal dose calculation, hearing and nerve effects, and the separate radiotherapy consent covering mouth, saliva, skin, dental, jaw and swallowing effects. Confirm actual urgent contacts and use teach-back. This draft does not authorise treatment.

patient_education: Contact oncology promptly for fever, shivering, sudden illness, unusual bleeding, persistent vomiting, much less urine or inability to drink. Report worsening hearing, numbness or tingling before the next dose. Severe breathing difficulty, collapse or severe chest pain is an emergency.
special_support: This carboplatin regimen has high sickness risk. Take the prescribed prevention and rescue medicines on their written schedule. Call if nausea or vomiting prevents drinking.
Tell the team early if swallowing, appetite, pain or taste changes reduce intake. A dietitian can agree practical food, drink or feeding support with you. Do not wait for substantial weight loss.
Agree a mouth-care plan and tell your dentist about previous or current cancer treatment. Arrange oncology advice before dental procedures, particularly after head and neck radiation.
Ask for speech and language therapy if swallowing or speech is difficult. Use the food textures, exercises and communication support advised for you; a general guide cannot establish safe swallowing.

Bring prescribed, over-the-counter and herbal medicines and supplements for review. Discuss fertility preservation and breastfeeding before treatment. Carboplatin can impair fertility. Do not breastfeed during treatment. The linked Irish product information advises contraception for women during treatment and at least six months afterwards; men should avoid fathering a child during treatment and at least three months afterwards. Confirm the actual product and personal advice.

priority_toxicities: Hearing / tinnitus: Report hearing change or ringing in the ears; previous platinum treatment increases risk.
Mouth / throat / saliva: Mouth pain, thick saliva, dry mouth or swallowing difficulty can limit drinking; seek help early.
Blood cells / infection: Fever, shivering, sudden illness, unusual bruising or bleeding needs prompt oncology advice.
Kidneys / fluids: Kidney tests guide the carboplatin dose. Much less urine, persistent vomiting or inability to drink needs urgent advice.
Nausea / appetite: Take the prescribed prevention and rescue medicines. Call if vomiting persists or fluids will not stay down.
Nerves / hands / feet: Report numbness, tingling, balance problems or difficulty with fine tasks; symptoms can persist.
Skin / treated area: Follow the radiation team’s skin plan. Report painful redness, peeling or a wound that is not healing.
Teeth / jaw / swallowing: Dental review, nutrition and swallowing support continue through recovery. Report jaw stiffness, weight loss or choking.

regimen_profiles.context_label: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Nivolumab every 2 weeks for head and neck cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Nivolumab aims to control head and neck cancer that has returned or spread, relieve symptoms and help some people live longer. Benefit and side effects are reviewed for you.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Recurrent or metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck after platinum treatment; the cancer cannot be treated with curative local therapy and has progressed or returned within six months of the last platinum dose.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD-1 on immune cells, helping them recognise and attack cancer. It can also cause inflammation in healthy organs.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Nivolumab is given as 240 mg through a vein over 30 minutes OR 600 mg as an injection under the skin over 3–5 minutes, on Day 1 every 2 weeks. Your team selects one formulation; these doses are not interchangeable milligram for milligram. Allow extra time for safety checks, preparation and observation. Treatment continues until the cancer progresses or side effects become unacceptable, with individual benefit and safety review. There is no fixed number of cycles in this head and neck treatment course.
key_points: Recurrent or metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck after platinum treatment; the cancer cannot be treated with curative local therapy and has progressed or returned within six months of the last platinum dose.

Nivolumab is given as 240 mg through a vein over 30 minutes OR 600 mg as an injection under the skin over 3–5 minutes, on Day 1 every 2 weeks. Your team selects one formulation; these doses are not interchangeable milligram for milligram. Allow extra time for safety checks, preparation and observation. Treatment continues until the cancer progresses or side effects become unacceptable, with individual benefit and safety review. There is no fixed number of cycles in this head and neck treatment course.
Full blood count, kidney and liver tests, glucose and thyroid tests; review autoimmune disease, transplants, previous immune side effects and all medicines.
Full blood count, kidney and liver tests and glucose before every 2-week cycle. Thyroid tests once a month and when indicated; cortisol when clinically indicated.

Keep reporting new symptoms after treatment ends. Immune side effects require monitoring for at least five months after the last dose. Steroid tapers, hormone replacement or specialist review may continue longer. Scans and examinations follow your individual response and follow-up plan.

priority_toxicities: Hormones / nervous system: Severe headache, confusion, weakness, dizziness or marked thirst need prompt advice.
Lungs: New cough or breathlessness can signal inflammation or another urgent cause.
Heart: Chest pain, racing heartbeat or fainting needs urgent assessment.
Liver: Yellow eyes/skin or dark urine may signal inflammation; tests also check the liver.

Skin: Report a spreading rash, painful skin, blisters or peeling promptly.
